From f2e97dc126b712c0d21219ed0c42710006c1cf52 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: John Fastabend <john.fastabend@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Feb 2020 21:44:37 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Selftests build error in sockmap_basic.c
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Fix following build error. We could push a tcp.h header into one of the
include paths, but I think its easy enough to simply pull in the three
defines we need here. If we end up using more of tcp.h at some point
we can pull it in later.

/home/john/git/bpf/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/prog_tests/sockmap_basic.c: In function ‘connected_socket_v4’:
/home/john/git/bpf/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/prog_tests/sockmap_basic.c:20:11: error: ‘TCP_REPAIR_ON’ undeclared (first use in this function)
  repair = TCP_REPAIR_ON;
           ^
/home/john/git/bpf/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/prog_tests/sockmap_basic.c:20:11: note: each undeclared identifier is reported only once for each function it appears in
/home/john/git/bpf/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/prog_tests/sockmap_basic.c:29:11: error: ‘TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP’ undeclared (first use in this function)
  repair = TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP;

Then with fix,

$ ./test_progs -n 44
#44/1 sockmap create_update_free:OK
#44/2 sockhash create_update_free:OK
#44 sockmap_basic:OK

Fixes: 5d3919a953c3c ("selftests/bpf: Test freeing sockmap/sockhash with a socket in it")
Signed-off-by: John Fastabend <john.fastabend@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Jakub Sitnicki <jakub@cloudflare.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/158131347731.21414.12120493483848386652.stgit@john-Precision-5820-Tower

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/prog_tests/sockmap_basic.c b/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/prog_tests/sockmap_basic.c
index 07f5b462c2ef..aa43e0bd210c 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/prog_tests/sockmap_basic.c
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/prog_tests/sockmap_basic.c
@@ -3,6 +3,11 @@
 
 #include "test_progs.h"
 
+#define TCP_REPAIR		19	/* TCP sock is under repair right now */
+
+#define TCP_REPAIR_ON		1
+#define TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP	-1	/* Turn off without window probes */
+
 static int connected_socket_v4(void)
 {
 	struct sockaddr_in addr = {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `tools/testing/selftests/bpf/prog_tests/sockmap_basic.c`**
- Added three `#define` statements to define the constants `TCP_REPAIR`, `TCP_REPAIR_ON`, and `TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP`. 
  - `#define TCP_REPAIR 19` 
  - `#define TCP_REPAIR_ON 1`
  - `#define TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP -1` 

These definitions were added to resolve build errors related to the undeclared identifiers `TCP_REPAIR_ON` and `TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP` in the function `connected_socket_v4`.

### Relationships
The modifications in `sockmap_basic.c` directly address the build errors encountered when compiling the self-tests for the BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) program. By defining the necessary constants locally within the file, the patch ensures that the function `connected_socket_v4` can compile successfully without needing to include the `tcp.h` header file at this time. This change is a temporary fix that allows the tests to run while maintaining the option to include the header later if more TCP-related functionality is needed.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
repair = TCP_REPAIR_ON;
repair = TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP;
```
Reason:
The identifiers `TCP_REPAIR_ON` and `TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP` are used in the `connected_socket_v4` function without being declared, leading to compilation errors. These identifiers were expected to be defined in the `tcp.h` header file, which was not included in the source file.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define TCP_REPAIR_ON		1
#define TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP	-1	/* Turn off without window probes */
```
Reason:
By defining `TCP_REPAIR_ON` and `TCP_REPAIR_OFF_NO_WP` directly in the `sockmap_basic.c` file, the code now has the necessary identifiers available, allowing the function to compile successfully without needing to include the `tcp.h` header file.
